Note::scalar¶

Back to Note API Reference

Signature¶

std::string_view Note::scalar() const

Borrow The Only Cell¶

scalar() returns the receiver’s sole cell as a non-owning std::string_view. Its contract is about cardinality, not rank: any defined Note with numel() == 1 is accepted. A true rank-zero scalar, a shape [1] vector, a shape [1, 1] matrix, and a shape [1, 1, 1] tensor therefore all have a scalar projection. This is deliberately broader than is_scalar(), which asks whether the Note has rank zero.

The returned view names the exact stored bytes. No string is allocated, no terminating zero is appended, and no UTF-8 validation is performed. An empty text cell is consequently a valid scalar result with size() == 0; it must not be confused with a zero-element Note, which has no cell to return.

Because the view borrows the packed text arena, it remains valid only while a Note or TextRef still owns that arena. Use owned() for a zero-copy handle that keeps storage alive, or construct std::string(n.scalar()) when an independent mutable copy is wanted. The lookup itself is constant-time and allocation-free.

Example 1: Read A Rank-Zero Scalar¶

const auto n = pluss::note::make("alpha");
std::cout << "rank0=" << n.scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

rank0=alpha

Example 2: Cardinality, Not Rank, Controls Acceptance¶

const auto vector = pluss::note::make({"beta"});
const auto matrix = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"gamma"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 2>{1, 1});
const auto tensor = pluss::note::make(
    std::vector<std::string>{"delta"},
    std::array<std::int64_t, 3>{1, 1, 1});

std::cout << "rank1=" << vector.scalar() << '\n'
          << "rank2=" << matrix.scalar() << '\n'
          << "rank3=" << tensor.scalar() << '\n';

Output¶

rank1=beta
rank2=gamma
rank3=delta

This is useful after a selection that leaves one cell but intentionally keeps one or more size-one axes.

Example 3: Empty Text Is Still One Cell¶

const auto text = pluss::note::make("").scalar();
std::cout << "empty text bytes=" << text.size() << '\n';

Output¶

empty text bytes=0

Example 4: Preserve The Result Past The Source Lifetime¶

std::string retained;
{
  const auto temporary = pluss::note::make({"keep", "copy"});
  retained = std::string(temporary.vector()[1]);
}
std::cout << "owned copy after source=" << retained << '\n';

Output¶

owned copy after source=copy

For a one-cell Note, temporary.owned() avoids copying while retaining shared ownership. The explicit std::string above illustrates the independent-copy choice that also applies to scalar().

Example 5: Multiple Cells And Absence Reject¶

auto report = [](std::string_view label, const pluss::Note& n) {
  try { (void)n.scalar(); }
  catch (const pluss::Error&) { std::cout << label << ": rejected\n"; }
};

report("scalar two cells", pluss::note::make({"a", "b"}));
report("scalar undefined", pluss::Note::undefined());

Output¶

scalar two cells: rejected
scalar undefined: rejected

See Also¶

  • owned: retain the sole cell with shared ownership.

  • at: borrow one cell by flat position from a multi-cell Note.

  • is_scalar: test rank zero rather than one-cell cardinality.

  • vector: borrow every cell in row-major order.
